mf-contrescarpe.title: Rue Mouffetard
mf-contrescarpe.note: The market street below the square, photographed the years Hemingway lived above it.

mf-cardinal-lemoine.title: Passport photograph
mf-cardinal-lemoine.note: Hemingway at twenty-four, the year he was living at this address.

mf-descartes.title: Rue Descartes
mf-descartes.note: The street of the writing room, as it looked when he climbed the stairs each morning.

mf-saint-michel.title: Le Pont Saint-Michel
mf-saint-michel.note: The bridge and quays beside the café, painted from a window above the river.

mf-odeon.title: Sylvia Beach at Shakespeare and Company
mf-odeon.note: The bookseller who lent him books on trust, in her shop.

mf-luxembourg.title: Le Golfe de Marseille vu de L'Estaque
mf-luxembourg.note: From the Caillebotte bequest, which hung in the Musée du Luxembourg in the 1920s — among the Cézannes he came here to study.

mf-fleurus.title: Portrait of Gertrude Stein
mf-fleurus.note: Stein, painted in the years her Saturday salon made this address famous.

mf-notre-dame-des-champs.title: Ernest, Hadley and Bumby
mf-notre-dame-des-champs.note: The family who lived above the sawmill, photographed in Schruns, Austria.

mf-closerie.title: La Closerie des Lilas
mf-closerie.note: The terrace under the trees, a decade and a half before he wrote there.

sr-negre-toulouse.title: Café scene
sr-negre-toulouse.note: Montparnasse café life by one of its own regulars, a painter Hemingway also wrote about.

sr-bal-musette.title: À Sainte-Geneviève, 46 Rue de la Montagne-Sainte-Geneviève
sr-bal-musette.note: The same street number as the novel's dance hall, photographed fifteen years earlier.

sr-select.title: Café du Dôme, Montparnasse
sr-select.note: The terrace across the boulevard from the Select: the crowd the novel moves through.

sr-dingo.title: F. Scott Fitzgerald
sr-dingo.note: The writer Hemingway first met at this bar in 1925.

sr-crillon.title: Place de la Concorde
sr-crillon.note: The square outside the hotel where Jake waits.

sr-lecomte.title: Quai d'Anjou, 6h du matin
sr-lecomte.note: The quay of Madame Lecomte's at six in the morning, the year before the novel is set.
